newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Mbeki to take up trade deal in Europe.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mbeki to take up trade deal in Europe.

text.p: South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki will press the European Union to change its stance in trade talks during an eight-nation trip to Europe starting on Wednesday, a trade official said on Monday.

"The deputy president will be calling for a change in the approach that the EU has taken in their mandate and he will be asking them to take a very different view of the role of the South African Customs Union (SACU) and the Southern African Development Community (SADC)," Faizel Ismail, chief director of foreign trade relations, told a news briefing.

Ismail said the EU position did not take sufficient account of the impact which a trade deal with South Africa would have in terms of loss of revenue and diversion of trade on its fellow- members of the SACU and SADC.
These are Angola, Botswana, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Lesotho, Swaziland, Tanzania, Zambia, Zimbabwe and Mauritius.
"The EU mandate has been criticised widely, the agriculture sector has been most concerned because 40 percent of agricultural trade has been excluded," Ismail said.

Mbeki, heir apparent to President Nelson Mandela who steps down in 1999, starts his tour in Germany and will also visit Italy, Sweden, Norway, France, Ireland, Belgium and Britain before returning on November 19. He will attend the World Food Summit in Italy on November 15.
"Our view is that trade negotiations should be linked to wider development issues," Ismail said.

"This agreement will have to be reciprocal... We have consistently called for this reciprocity to be on an asymetrical basis. We should be granted quicker access to the EU market than they are to the South African market," he said.
